x: This team consisted of Doubleday, Ogilvie, Roberts and True, the two first-named taking their first team prizes in Club teams. Our "A" team was placed third; and so we may be considered to have had an excellent Saturday afternoon out.
Bentley, Rickards, Snell, Harley, and Doubleday retired (and others).
Doubleday is another to have changed over and shows great promise; while in Colin Sutton we have one who has competed with some distinction in cycling road races.
Bridger, Heather, Thaxter, Roberts, Doubleday, Snell, and others, supporting Bert Clayton, our Eastleigh member, who may win the individual title, is certainly a team of possibilities.

Doubleday, finished inside ten hours and so qualify for second-class team medals. Doubleday improved an hour and a half over the previous year's performance, which was incidentally his first walking race.

Clayton, Heather, Roberts, Thaxter, Doubleday, Bridger, Goold, Elliott, East, Snell and others have great potentialities, and with conscientious, steady training, we may expect a team which will represent the Club with credit.

These two were still leading at the top of the hills, with Roberts leading Thaxter and Doubleday for third place. Going round the common again, Heather was a few yards in front, but there was little to choose between them when the hills were tackled again.

Our "B" team (Clark, Doubleday, Roberts and True) managed to get in the prize-winners again, taking second handicap team prize. Brunning, Jones and Little also gave us encouraging performances, and their constant support of open races is an excellent testimony to their keenness and club-spirit.
Roberts, Doubleday, Clark and Heather, of the "B" team, walked well and comprised the second handicap team. Eddie Heather's forward walking, his best to date, earned third individual handicap prize.

Jack Flower.—Belated news that he is in Iraq and is sporting " one Pip and a Sam Browne." From Exeter.—News has just reached us that Doubleday (" Doub ") is safe and returning to London as soon as possible.
The race was also important for the re-appearance of Gordon Doubleday, who celebrated his return to the London area with a run over Marathon distance.

The handicap team race was won by our "A" Team with Demmon, Newson, Hall and Doubleday with an aggregate time of 206m.2s. Surrey W.C. were 2nd and Woodford Green 3rd.

John Knifton was 24th in Section A Barnes, Belderson, Beecham and Keown, 6th 7th 30th and 32nd respectively in Section B; Eglington, Cameron, McLennan, Duncan,Wilson and Doubleday between 18 and 62 in Section C; Bushman, East and Logan 14th,15th and 34th in Section D.

On April 29th 1944 Etienne (immediately becoming known as Steve) was elected a member of Belgrave Harriers and he found himself running alongside such notables as Carter, Cohen, Shields and Doubleday.
